Requirement: Provide a bounded orchestration overlay for one synthetic diagnostic-closure episode, making verified workflow state, owner, blocker and next action visible without replacing source systems.
Business rule: Source systems remain authoritative for patient, encounter, diagnostic and source operational records; ContinuumOS owns internal workflow visibility and evidence only.
Acceptance criteria: A walkthrough identifies the current canonical state, verified linkage status, owner, blocker and next task without presenting ContinuumOS as the source clinical record.
Source: Sprint 3 MVP scope freeze CAP-01/CAP-02; Sprint 4 AP-02
Notes: Baseline candidate; screen coverage in Part 3.

Actor: Clinic physician; Care Coordinator; Referral Coordinator
State: Result Available; Follow-up Decision Required; Next Step Confirmed
Requirement: Maintain human-controlled clinical acknowledgement, follow-up direction, referral decision and workflow closure.
Business rule: No rule or AI output may perform a gated clinical, identity, financial or closure decision.
Acceptance criteria: Each gated action shows the authorised actor, required evidence and attributable record; unauthorised actions are blocked or represented as failure behaviour.
Source: Sprint 3 decision-rights matrix S3-DR04/S3-DR05/S3-DR07/S3-DR18; Sprint 4 AP-06
Notes: Closure evidence and actor matrix in Part 2.

State: Patient Match Failed; Encounter Missing; Result Incomplete; Duplicate Event Suspected; Clinician Unavailable
Requirement: Make material workflow failures visible, owned and recoverable through a safe-return condition.
Business rule: An exception never silently creates a valid episode, successful source write or state advance.
Acceptance criteria: Each represented exception has reason, owner, safe action, prohibited action, return condition and audit evidence.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-08/CAP-11; Sprint 2 failure-path map; Sprint 4 event recovery rules
Notes: Detailed rules in Part 2.

Actor: Clinic physician; Care Coordinator; Referral Coordinator
Requirement: Allow only source-linked episode summaries and post-approval referral-handoff drafts as optional human-reviewed assistance.
Business rule: AI is non-blocking; it may not diagnose, determine urgency, match identity or complete/approve/send/accept/reject a workflow action.
Acceptance criteria: Both assists visibly show draft status, source references/versions, uncertainty and a recorded human disposition; normal workflow remains available when AI is unavailable.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-10/CAP-12; Sprint 4 AI service cards
Notes: Controlled sample outputs only; no model claim.

Requirement: Provide a simulated clinician-only SMART launch into synthetic Asha Mehta context and retrieve approved minimum source context after authorisation.
Business rule: Use read-only synthetic FHIR-shaped resources; do not retain raw tokens, secrets or full authorisation responses.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype shows launch context, authorised clinician identity/context and minimum retrieved source references; it does not imply a live connection.
Source: Sprint 3 integration flow; Sprint 4 SMART launch sequence; S4-AD02/S4-AD12
Notes: Operations access is separate and role-authorised.

Requirement: Stop protected retrieval when launch, authorisation or endpoint access fails and preserve an attributable technical condition.
Business rule: Do not display protected data, retain credentials or present failed retrieval as source success.
Acceptance criteria: A failure path presents the condition, last verified safe state, support/escalation route and no false episode advancement.
Source: Sprint 1 E13; Sprint 2 exception workflow Integration Unavailable; Sprint 3 integration flow; Sprint 4 SMART failure rules
Notes: Represented failure; no live OAuth.

Requirement: Require verified patient, encounter, order and applicable event references before attaching an episode.
Business rule: Uncertain or conflicting linkage is quarantined for accountable human reconciliation; source records are not altered.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype makes linkage status and evidence visible and routes uncertainty to the approved exception state rather than silently attaching the episode.
Source: Sprint 3 JTBD-07/CAP-01; Sprint 4 AP-03/EVT-04
Notes: No autonomous matching.

Requirement: Show the active episode workspace with current canonical state, verified linkage status, owner, age/due context, blocker and next task.
Business rule: Operational visibility does not confer clinical, identity or financial authority.
Acceptance criteria: For the synthetic episode, all seven required workspace elements are visible and unresolved work is distinguishable from completed work.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-01/CAP-05
Notes: SLA values remain illustrative; no performance claim.

Actor: Diagnostic operations user; authorised reporting professional; Clinic physician
State: Order Created; Order Accepted; Diagnostic Scheduled; Diagnostic Completed; Result Available; Result Incomplete; Amended Result Received
Requirement: Distinguish diagnostic operational milestones from report availability, current report version and clinical review.
Business rule: Result Available requires the approved synthetic-fixture status/version, configured result references and separate completion evidence; availability is not acknowledgement.
Acceptance criteria: A walkthrough distinguishes every listed milestone, shows the current report version and routes missing/conflicting evidence to Result Incomplete.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-03; Sprint 4 S4-AD08; EVT-06 to EVT-10
Notes: Source-side reporting remains authoritative.

Requirement: Allow only the authorised Clinic physician to acknowledge the current report version after source review.
Business rule: Acknowledgement records actor, timestamp and current report version; amended/corrected versions require renewed review and acknowledgement.
Acceptance criteria: The acknowledgement control is unavailable to unauthorised roles; an amended report retains earlier acknowledgement as history only and presents renewed review work.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-04; Sprint 4 report-version change contract; EVT-10
Notes: No AI or rule shortcut.

Actor: Care Coordinator; authorised clinical escalation owner
State: All active canonical states; Clinician Unavailable
Requirement: Show a current accountable owner, age/due information, blocker and escalation route for each active task.
Business rule: Deterministic rules may flag/route missing or overdue ownership; they cannot acknowledge, choose a pathway or close work.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype shows an owner and next action for active work and exposes an exception/escalation when ownership is missing, expired or unavailable.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-05/CAP-11; JTBD-15
Notes: Timing thresholds are proposed configuration, not universal SLA.

Requirement: Require the Clinic physician to record clinic management, day-care referral or hospital escalation before downstream handoff preparation.
Business rule: AI cannot choose or approve the direction or determine urgency.
Acceptance criteria: Only the three approved directions are available; the selected direction, authorised actor and supporting rationale/evidence reference are attributable.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-06; Sprint 4 EVT-11
Notes: Urgent escalation financial branch remains D12/T11U policy-dependent.

Requirement: Allow the Referral Coordinator to prepare and route a complete handoff only after a human-approved referral/escalation direction.
Business rule: Clinic physician approves clinical content where applicable; a draft is not a package or referral; source records are not written.
Acceptance criteria: The handoff view distinguishes draft, package preparation and routing; required fields, destination, owner and missing evidence are visible before routing.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-12; Sprint 4 EVT-12/EVT-13; AI-02
Notes: Receiving acceptance remains separate.

Requirement: Record formal receiving-team acceptance or rejection with receiving role, destination and timeframe evidence.
Business rule: Receiving-team authority is distinct from specialist review; rejection does not automatically redirect the referral.
Acceptance criteria: A response records acceptance/rejection, accountable receiving role, destination and timeframe; rejection returns visible human follow-up work.
Source: Sprint 3 JTBD-09/CAP-07; Sprint 4 EVT-14
Notes: No independent facility booking.

Actor: Care Coordinator; authorised communication owner; patient/caregiver where applicable
Requirement: Allow the Care Coordinator to record Next Step Confirmed only after required pathway evidence is visible.
Business rule: Confirmation requires human direction, applicable handoff/receiving evidence, accountable owner, timeframe and approved communication; delivery and explicit confirmation remain distinct where policy requires confirmation.
Acceptance criteria: AC-FR-11-01 to AC-FR-11-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 T11/T11U; Sprint 3 CAP-07; Sprint 4 EVT-16 to EVT-18
Notes: D12 remains represent-only policy context; scoped closure is FR-30.

State: Patient Match Failed; Encounter Missing; Result Incomplete; Duplicate Event Suspected; Clinician Unavailable; Referral Rejected
Requirement: Provide an exception queue and detail view containing reason, owner, safe action, prohibited action, safe-return condition and audit trail.
Business rule: Exception resolution is performed by the accountable human role; the Care Coordinator coordinates but does not gain clinical or identity authority.
Acceptance criteria: Each represented failure path displays required fields and an explicit return-to-last-verified-state or human-resolution path.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-08; Sprint 2 failure-path map; Sprint 4 recovery matrix
Notes: Exact screen treatment in Part 3.

State: All active canonical states; exception states
Requirement: Detect missing owner, overdue acknowledgement, missing handoff evidence, duplicate/incomplete data, stale work and unavailable service using deterministic workflow rules.
Business rule: Detection creates visible task/exception evidence only; it cannot make a clinical, identity, financial, referral or closure decision.
Acceptance criteria: Each represented condition has a visible reason, owner and safe return condition; no AI anomaly-detection claim is made.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-11; Sprint 4 S4-AD05
Notes: Rule thresholds documented in Part 2.

Requirement: Present attributable, append-oriented workflow and audit history for material state changes, human decisions, AI activity, exceptions, communications, corrections and recovery.
Business rule: Corrections create linked entries; failed/unavailable source actions are recorded as such and never as success.
Acceptance criteria: Timeline entries show actor/source, timestamp, event/outcome and appropriate source/version reference; corrections preserve earlier history.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-09; Sprint 4 audit contract; EVT-01 to EVT-22
Notes: Target behaviour; no immutable-store claim.

Requirement: Provide a source-linked episode-summary draft only after verified linkage and approved minimum source evidence are available.
Business rule: Output is orientation-only, includes source versions and uncertainty, and may be accepted for orientation, corrected, rejected, discarded or superseded; it has no direct state effect.
Acceptance criteria: The sample summary visibly labels draft status, source links and uncertainty; reviewer disposition is recorded and source review remains available.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-10; Sprint 4 AI-01/EVT-20
Notes: Controlled synthetic demonstration; non-blocking.

Requirement: Provide an editable source-linked referral-handoff draft only after a valid human referral/escalation direction.
Business rule: The draft may not create, send, approve, accept, reject, redirect or cancel a referral; stale inputs require regeneration or source-based human review.
Acceptance criteria: The sample draft shows required-field completeness, source links/versions and a human review disposition before package preparation.
Source: Sprint 3 CAP-12; Sprint 4 AI-02/EVT-20
Notes: Controlled synthetic demonstration; no model call.

Requirement: Limit synthetic source reads, internal workflow data, audit evidence and AI inputs to minimum necessary information for the stated workflow job.
Business rule: Do not retain raw SMART/OAuth data, secrets, full authorisation responses, unverified candidates or full longitudinal clinical content.
Acceptance criteria: Displayed source-context and AI/audit examples contain only approved synthetic minimum data and references; prohibited sensitive artefacts are absent.
Source: Sprint 3 permissions assumptions; Sprint 4 AP-09/AI cards
Notes: Prototype uses synthetic Asha Mehta data only.

Requirement: Keep source-system authority, internal-task separation and no-source-write boundary explicit in all prototype behaviours.
Business rule: The six source FHIR-shaped resources are read-only; internal/simulated continuum_task is separate and is not claimed as FHIR-conformant.
Acceptance criteria: No screen or scenario presents a ContinuumOS source-record edit or source write-back; internal workflow actions are labelled as such.
Source: Sprint 3 FHIR map/integration flow; Sprint 4 S4-AD02/S4-AD03/S4-AD13
Notes: Technical representation only.

Requirement: Ensure represented duplicate, retry, correction and outage behaviours preserve the last verified state and do not advance work twice.
Business rule: Use semantic event identity and linked correction/recovery evidence; restored service must not replay an unverified action.
Acceptance criteria: Failure scenarios visibly distinguish pending, failed, recovered and duplicate conditions and avoid duplicate transition or success presentation.
Source: Sprint 4 event catalogue and recovery rules; AP-10
Notes: No broker or exactly-once implementation claim.

Requirement: Use a simulated SMART-on-FHIR launch and synthetic FHIR R4-shaped Patient, Encounter, ServiceRequest, DiagnosticReport, Observation and Practitioner resources.
Business rule: SMART is clinician-only; operations use separately authorised access; candidate scopes are read-only.
Acceptance criteria: Prototype documentation and screens identify simulated/read-only access and use only the six approved source-resource types.
Source: Sprint 3 FHIR map/permissions; Sprint 4 SMART sequence/fixtures
Notes: No live conformance claim.

Requirement: Represent internal workflow tasks, exceptions and audit evidence separately from synthetic source resources.
Business rule: Internal task/workflow evidence may support orchestration only and cannot silently correct or overwrite a source record.
Acceptance criteria: Prototype labels internal task/exception/audit records as ContinuumOS orchestration evidence and preserves source references/versions.
Source: Sprint 3 integration flow; Sprint 4 S4-AD03/S4-AD13
Notes: Data and screen-field mapping in Part 2.

Requirement: Create an internal orchestration episode only when a verified source diagnostic order and verified linkage evidence are available.
Business rule: ContinuumOS records the source order; it does not create the clinical order or silently attach uncertain patient/encounter context.
Acceptance criteria: A verified source order creates a visible internal episode with source order reference and linkage status; uncertainty routes to Patient Match Failed or Encounter Missing.
Source: Sprint 1 T01/E01/E02; Sprint 2 DR01/DR02/operating control Order Created
Notes: Closes the episode-initiation gap identified in Part 1 review.

Requirement: Record diagnostic-provider acceptance from verified source evidence and make outstanding clarification visible.
Business rule: Only the diagnostic operations user/source system accepts diagnostic work; ContinuumOS records the event and cannot accept on the provider's behalf.
Acceptance criteria: A verified acceptance event updates visible operational status with actor, timestamp, reason where present and source reference; absent or rejected evidence remains unresolved.
Source: Sprint 1 T01; Sprint 2 DR04/operating control Order Accepted
Notes: Acceptance remains distinct from scheduling.

Requirement: Display verified appointment or diagnostic-slot status and the operational disposition for scheduled, rescheduled, cancelled or no-show work.
Business rule: ContinuumOS displays source appointment status and tasks; it cannot confirm attendance, infer completion or independently schedule care.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype distinguishes scheduled, cancelled, no-show and rescheduling context from Diagnostic Completed and retains order reference, status history and owner.
Source: Sprint 1 T02; Sprint 2 DR05/operating control Diagnostic Scheduled; exception workflow
Notes: Represent-only scheduling interaction; status/context is in scope.

Requirement: Record diagnostic completion from verified source evidence and create visible overdue-result follow-up when a current result does not arrive.
Business rule: Completion is not result availability. An overdue result remains in Diagnostic Completed with escalation; Integration Unavailable is used only when an outage is evidenced.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype shows verified completion evidence, source status and an overdue-result action without presenting a result or closing the episode.
Source: Sprint 1 T03; Sprint 2 DR06/operating control Diagnostic Completed; exception workflow Result never arrives
Notes: No inference of source outage or result availability.

Requirement: Create and display an acknowledgement task for the current report version when Result Available is established.
Business rule: The task contains the owner, due/age context, current report version and source links; it does not clinically interpret the report or acknowledge it.
Acceptance criteria: Result Available creates visible Clinical Review Pending work for the authorised Clinic physician; the task becomes stale and re-review is required when the current report version changes.
Source: Sprint 1 T04/T05; Sprint 2 DR07/DR18 and operating controls Result Available/Clinical Review Pending
Notes: Separates availability from review and acknowledgement.

State: Follow-up Decision Required; Next Step Confirmed
Requirement: When clinic management is selected, record the human direction and establish the accountable next-step owner, timeframe, task and required communication evidence before confirmation.
Business rule: Clinic management is a valid human-selected path; it is not a default outcome and cannot be inferred by ContinuumOS or AI.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype presents a clinic-management path with recorded physician direction, owner, timeframe, next task and applicable communication evidence before Next Step Confirmed.
Source: Sprint 1 T08/T11/T14; Sprint 2 happy-path steps 8-9 and operating controls
Notes: Closes the explicit clinic-management branch gap.

Actor: Billing/pre-authorisation user; authorised financial decision-maker; Care Coordinator
State: Financial Readiness Pending; Payer Information Missing; Authorisation Denied
Requirement: Represent financial readiness as a visible dependency after applicable clinical/referral prerequisites, including the approved urgent-escalation exception.
Business rule: ContinuumOS does not infer coverage or authorise finances. For urgent human-approved hospital escalation, Next Step Confirmed may be recorded while Financial Readiness Pending remains visible and unresolved under D12/T11U.
Acceptance criteria: Not a Sprint 6 acceptance item; retain only as future/represent-only traceability.
Source: Sprint 1 T12/T13/T11U/E10/E11/E12; Sprint 2 DR15/DR16/DR17 and exception workflow
Notes: Deferred from clickable MVP; no payer or authorisation workflow build.

Actor: Authorised communication owner; Clinic physician; Care Coordinator
Requirement: Record applicable approved patient/caregiver communication separately from delivery and explicit confirmation evidence.
Business rule: The authorised sender and any physician approval for clinically contextual content must be attributable. Delivery alone does not prove understanding or confirmation where confirmation is required.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype distinguishes approved communication, sender, delivery status and applicable explicit confirmation; closure checks show which evidence is required for the pathway.
Source: Sprint 1 T14/D17; Sprint 2 DR14/DR19 and operating control Next Step Confirmed; Sprint 4 AP-10
Notes: Does not introduce a patient-facing workflow.

Actor: Diagnostic operations user; Clinic physician; Care Coordinator
Requirement: When an amended or corrected current report arrives, preserve prior acknowledgement as historical evidence, create renewed review work and flag dependent direction/handoff/communication for human reassessment.
Business rule: A prior acknowledgement cannot satisfy the new version. No downstream action is automatically cancelled, redirected or resent.
Acceptance criteria: The amended-result scenario shows new version context, re-review work and visible reassessment flags while retaining prior audit history.
Source: Sprint 1 E05/E06; Sprint 2 exception workflow; Sprint 4 report-version change contract
Notes: Expands the version rule beyond acknowledgement alone.

Actor: Diagnostic operations user; Care Coordinator; Clinic physician
State: Result Incomplete; Integration Unavailable; Diagnostic Scheduled; Diagnostic Completed
Requirement: Represent cancellation, no-show, test-not-performed, diagnostic-provider order rejection and overdue/no-result as distinct operational conditions with owner, reason and safe human next action.
Business rule: No operational condition may be treated as completion, result availability, referral direction or closure. A new clinical direction remains human-owned.
Acceptance criteria: Not a Sprint 6 acceptance item unless a scenario is explicitly selected in Part 3.
Source: Sprint 1 E03/E04/E07; Sprint 2 exception workflow and operating controls
Notes: Deferred from clickable MVP; generic exception handling remains FR-12/FR-13.

Actor: Receiving team; Referral Coordinator; Clinic physician
Requirement: When the Receiving team rejects a referral/handoff, record the rejection reason and return visible work to the Clinic physician for a new human follow-up direction.
Business rule: ContinuumOS, AI and the Referral Coordinator cannot automatically redirect the referral or choose an alternative clinical pathway.
Acceptance criteria: The prototype records receiving response and reason, preserves the original handoff history, and returns the episode to Follow-up Decision Required for physician action.
Source: Sprint 1 E08/E09; Sprint 2 DR11 and exception workflow Referral rejected
Notes: Completes the rejection recovery branch.

Requirement: When represented financial authorisation is denied, keep the denial evidence visible and require a Clinic physician to record any alternative clinical pathway.
Business rule: Financial denial does not independently confirm a next step, authorise care or let AI select an alternative.
Acceptance criteria: Not a Sprint 6 acceptance item; retain only as future/represent-only traceability.
Source: Sprint 1 E11/E12; Sprint 2 DR16/DR17 and exception workflow Authorisation denied
Notes: Deferred from clickable MVP; financial-denial recovery remains a roadmap control.

Requirement: As a Clinic physician, I want the verified source order and current report context visible so that I can make and record the required human clinical direction without relying on an AI output.
Business rule: Clinical order creation and direction remain human-controlled; source records remain authoritative.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough covers verified order context and an attributable physician choice of clinic management, day-care referral or hospital escalation.
Source: Sprint 1 T01/T08; Sprint 2 DR01/DR10
Notes: Maps to FR-17 and FR-08.

Requirement: As an Identity reconciliation reviewer, I want uncertain patient or encounter linkage quarantined with its source evidence so that I can confirm or reject attachment safely.
Business rule: No autonomous or silent attachment is permitted.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough shows a human resolution or rejection path with reviewer, timestamp and safe return condition.
Source: Sprint 1 E01/E02; Sprint 2 DR03
Notes: Maps to FR-03.

State: Order Accepted; Diagnostic Scheduled; Diagnostic Completed; Result Incomplete
Requirement: As a Diagnostic operations user, I want acceptance, scheduling, completion and operational exceptions shown separately so that workflow status reflects verified source reality.
Business rule: Operational status cannot be treated as report availability or clinical review.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough distinguishes acceptance, schedule, completion, incomplete/no-result and source evidence.
Source: Sprint 1 T01/T02/T03/E03/E04; Sprint 2 DR04/DR05/DR06
Notes: Maps to FR-18 through FR-20 and FR-26.

State: Result Available; Clinical Review Pending; Result Acknowledged; Amended Result Received
Requirement: As a Clinic physician, I want the current report version and my acknowledgement task clearly shown so that I can review and acknowledge the correct version and re-review amendments.
Business rule: AI cannot acknowledge or determine clinical significance; prior acknowledgement does not transfer to an amended version.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough shows Result Available, assigned review work, attributable acknowledgement and amended-version re-review.
Source: Sprint 1 T04/T05/T06/E05/E06; Sprint 2 DR08/DR09
Notes: Maps to FR-05, FR-06, FR-21 and FR-25.

Requirement: As a Care Coordinator, I want an active episode workspace and owned exception work so that I can coordinate blockers, ageing and evidence without taking clinical or identity decisions.
Business rule: Deterministic controls may flag and route; the Care Coordinator verifies evidence but does not decide clinical safety.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough shows state, owner, age, blocker, next task, exception reason and safe return condition.
Source: Sprint 1 D02/D10; Sprint 2 DR18/DR19 and operating controls
Notes: Maps to FR-04, FR-07, FR-12 and FR-13.

Requirement: As a Referral Coordinator, I want to prepare, review and route a complete handoff only after physician approval so that receiving-team responsibility can be tracked without AI sending or approving it.
Business rule: AI may draft after human direction only; a human approves package use and routing.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough shows approved direction, required fields, draft/package distinction, routing and rejection recovery.
Source: Sprint 1 T09/T10/E08; Sprint 2 DR12/DR13
Notes: Maps to FR-09, FR-16 and FR-27.

State: Referral Created; Referral Rejected; Referral Accepted
Requirement: As a Receiving-team user, I want to record acceptance or rejection with destination and timeframe so that downstream ownership is explicit.
Business rule: Receiving-team response is human-controlled and cannot be inferred or redirected automatically.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough records attributable acceptance/rejection, destination, timeframe and reason where rejected.
Source: Sprint 1 T10/E08/E09; Sprint 2 DR11
Notes: Maps to FR-10 and FR-27.

Requirement: As a Care Coordinator, I want to verify pathway-specific owner, timeframe, handoff and communication evidence so that I can record a confirmed next step and scoped workflow completion without claiming broader care completion.
Business rule: Communication delivery and explicit confirmation remain separate where applicable; closure is human-owned and cannot bypass an unresolved safety-blocking exception.
Acceptance criteria: Walkthrough shows the evidence checklist, the accountable closer and preserved audit trail for confirmation and completion.
Source: Sprint 1 T11/T14/D17; Sprint 2 DR19 and operating controls
Notes: Maps to FR-11, FR-22 and FR-24.

Requirement: Open and display a follow-up decision task when the current report version has been acknowledged and no direction is recorded.
Business rule: The task identifies the accountable Clinic physician, current report/version context and pathway options; task creation does not choose a direction or imply a clinical recommendation.
Acceptance criteria: An attributable acknowledgement creates visible Follow-up Decision Required work; the task remains pending until the Clinic physician records an approved direction.
Source: Sprint 1 T07; Sprint 2 operating controls Result Acknowledged/Follow-up Decision Required; DR10
Notes: Closes the explicit T07 transition gap identified in Part 1 validation.

Requirement: Allow the Care Coordinator to record Episode Completed only when the confirmed pathway has been handed off or clinic follow-up responsibility is clear and closure evidence is complete.
Business rule: Closure is human-owned, follows Next Step Confirmed, requires no unresolved safety-blocking exception and ends only the diagnostic-closure workflow—not broader patient care.
Acceptance criteria: AC-FR-30-01 to AC-FR-30-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 T14; Sprint 2 DR19/operating control Episode Completed; Sprint 4 EVT-22
Notes: Separated from FR-11 because closure has a distinct evidence gate.

Requirement: Establish Result Available only when the approved synthetic-fixture current report status/version, configured result references and separate completion evidence are present.
Business rule: Completion, scheduling and Observation presence alone do not establish result availability; missing or conflicting evidence routes to Result Incomplete.
Acceptance criteria: AC-FR-31-01 to AC-FR-31-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 T04/E04; Sprint 2 DR07; Sprint 4 S4-AD08/EVT-09
Notes: Separates the availability gate from general diagnostic milestone display.

Actor: Diagnostic operations user; Clinic physician; Care Coordinator
Requirement: Preserve the current report version and source provenance across review, downstream direction, handoff and communication evidence.
Business rule: A changed version marks dependent work stale for human reassessment; no prior acknowledgement or derived content silently transfers to the new version.
Acceptance criteria: AC-FR-32-01 to AC-FR-32-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 E05/E06; Sprint 2 DR07/DR09; Sprint 4 version-change contract
Notes: Separates version integrity from the result-availability gate.

Requirement: Record linked correction, supersession, failure and recovery evidence without destructively altering prior workflow history.
Business rule: A failed or unavailable source action is never represented as success; linked entries preserve logical event, actor, timestamp and source/version context.
Acceptance criteria: AC-FR-33-01 to AC-FR-33-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 D16/D17; Sprint 3 CAP-09; Sprint 4 audit contract/EVT-21
Notes: Separates audit correction/recovery from timeline visibility.

Requirement: The clickable prototype must support keyboard operation, visible focus, logical reading order, text alternatives and non-colour-only status/error meaning for all critical workflow actions.
Business rule: Accessibility support must not obscure human-control, exception or confirmation information.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-04-01 to AC-NFR-04-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Project-local design standards; Sprint 5 scope controls
Notes: Prototype accessibility requirement; detailed checks apply in Sprint 6.

Requirement: Show each role only the minimum workflow information and actions required for its approved responsibility.
Business rule: Role visibility does not confer clinical, identity, referral, financial or closure authority; source access remains read-only and scoped.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-05-01 to AC-NFR-05-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 3 permissions assumptions; Sprint 2 decision-rights matrix; Sprint 4 AP-08
Notes: Prototype demonstrates least-privilege behaviour; no production RBAC claim.

State: Integration Unavailable; Result Incomplete; Patient Match Failed
Requirement: Present errors and blocked states in plain language with the known condition, affected work, safe next action and accountable owner where applicable.
Business rule: Errors must not imply source success, conceal uncertainty or instruct a user to bypass a human gate.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-06-01 to AC-NFR-06-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 2 failure-path map; Sprint 4 recovery rules
Notes: Applies to represented failures only.

Requirement: Require the defined audit fields for material workflow, human-decision, AI-review, exception, communication, correction and recovery events.
Business rule: Required fields include event/state, timestamp, actor/source, applicable role/approval, source reference/version and correction/rejection/override evidence.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-07-01 to AC-NFR-07-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 1 success metrics Audit completeness; Sprint 4 audit contract
Notes: Requirement only; no achieved audit-completeness metric.

Actor: Clinic physician; Referral Coordinator; Care Coordinator
State: Result Acknowledged; Follow-up Decision Required; Referral Created; Next Step Confirmed; Episode Completed
Requirement: Require clear review and explicit confirmation before a user records a high-risk human-controlled action.
Business rule: The confirmation must show the action, current source/version context where applicable, authorised actor and the evidence that will be recorded; it must not substitute for source review.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-08-01 to AC-NFR-08-03 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 2 DR08 to DR19; Sprint 4 AP-06
Notes: Usability control, not an extra clinical approval.

Requirement: Provide an immediate visible response to a user action or an explicit loading/unavailable state in the clickable prototype.
Business rule: This is a prototype usability expectation, not a production performance SLA or latency claim.
Acceptance criteria: AC-NFR-09-01 to AC-NFR-09-02 in acceptance catalogue.
Source: Sprint 5 prototype-definition decision
Notes: No numeric performance target is claimed.
